title: Sales Enablement Prospect Kit — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Priya Sharma
body:
Overview:

This document is a consolidated prospect-facing sales enablement kit for Redwood Inference. It contains elevator messaging and positioning, concise competitive briefs, a recommended pitch-deck outline with talking points, pricing guidance and guardrails for commercial conversations, two short customer case studies for proof, and a security FAQ tailored for prospect security reviewers. Use this kit in discovery calls, executive briefings, and when preparing sales collateral for enterprise prospects.

1) Elevator positioning and messaging (top-line)

- Elevator pitch (30s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes high-performance, reliable LLM serving predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We help engineering teams ship LLM features with consistent latency, cost controls, and enterprise controls—without building a custom inference stack.
- Value pillars (one-liners):
  - Production-first performance: predictable latency & throughput with GPU-optimized runtime and smart routing.
  - Cost-control & economics: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations to reduce per-token cost.
  - Deployment flexibility: hosted API, reserved Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads.
  - Observability & reliability: token-level cost/latency breakdowns and rollout tooling (canary/A-B/fallback).

2) Target buyer profiles & pain signals

- Primary buyers: ML Engineers, Platform/ML infra teams, Product/Engineering leaders at AI-native startups and regulated enterprise product teams.
- Typical pain signals:
  1. High and variable LLM inference costs with unpredictable latency spikes.
  2. Growing staff time spent on model serving and ops rather than product features.
  3. Compliance or data residency requirements preventing hosted-only solutions.
  4. Lack of fine-grained observability to attribute cost/latency to prompts, routes, or models.

3) Competitive brief (concise comparisons and objections)

- Competitors covered: Major cloud-managed LLM endpoints (Cloud A endpoints), LLM API providers (Provider B/C), and self-hosted inference vendors (OpenInfra D).
- Differentiators (how to position):
  - vs Cloud-managed endpoints: Redwood provides predictable per-request latency with targeted kernel selection and smart routing to cheaper compatible model variants; call out our Dedicated pools and SLA-backed latency commitments.
  - vs LLM API providers: emphasize unit economics tooling (batching/caching/quantization profiles) and first-class private deployments (VPC/on-prem) for regulated customers.
  - vs self-hosted inference vendors: we offer unified developer API, observability, and managed Dedicated options to reduce ops burden while preserving private deployment choices.
- Common competitive objections & rebuttals:
  - Objection: "We can just host open models ourselves to save cost." Rebuttal: "Self-hosting often underestimates ops complexity (KV cache, batching, kernel selection, quantization trade-offs). Redwood reduces up-front build and ongoing operational costs and offers Reserved Dedicated to control spend while delivering predictable latency."
  - Objection: "Cloud vendor has tighter integration with our infra." Rebuttal: "We support private deployments and cloud-region routing and can integrate with your identity and KMS; many customers run hybrid topologies with us to keep control and leverage our runtime optimizations."

4) Pitch deck outline (recommended slides and speaker notes)

- Slide 1 — Title / Who we are: 1-line positioning + logo + presenter's contact.
- Slide 2 — Market context: growth of LLM usage, inference costs as a blocker for scaling features.
- Slide 3 — Customer problem: unpredictable latency, rising cost, ops burden, regulatory constraints.
- Slide 4 — Redwood solution at a glance: hosted API, Dedicated, Private + observability and cost controls.
- Slide 5 — Architecture diagram: quick visual showing client -> Redwood API -> routing to Hosted/Dedicated/Private with KV cache and fallback. (Speaker note: emphasize unified API.)
- Slide 6 — Performance & economics: representative latency percentiles, throughput for Dedicated pools, and typical cost savings examples from batching/caching.
- Slide 7 — Security & compliance: SOC 2, KMS integrations, VPC/private control plane, audit logging.
- Slide 8 — Case studies (two short examples).
- Slide 9 — Commercial options & sample pricing (see pricing guidance).
- Slide 10 — Implementation plan & timeline: POC (2–4 weeks), pilot (1–3 months), production rollout (1–3 months).
- Slide 11 — Next steps / tailored ask: POC kickoff, security questionnaire, or pricing approval.

5) Pricing guidance (talking points and guardrails)

- Pricing models: usage-based (hosted API per-token / per-embedding), reserved Dedicated (monthly/annual commits), enterprise Private (platform fee + support).
- Commercial playbook:
  1. Discovery: determine expected RPS, model family, average sequence length, and latency SLOs.
  2. Recommend mode: hosted for early stage/low needs; Dedicated for predictable throughput; Private for regulated data.
  3. Offer Pricing ranges (example talk tracks — examples only):
     - Hosted (pay-as-you-go): $0.0006–$0.003 per generated token (varies by model family).
     - Dedicated reserved: commitment-based pricing with 15%–45% discount vs hosted p95 unit costs, depending on commit term and utilization assumptions.
     - Private: platform + support pricing typically quoted as an ARR (starts ~ $250k ARR) depending on deployment complexity and SLAs.
- Discounting guidelines: for deals > $500k ARR or multi-year commitments, engage sales leadership and finance for structured discounts and milestone-based credits.
- Bundles & add-ons: longer observability retention, premium SLA, and compliance packages are add-ons priced separately.

6) Case studies (concise one-paragraph examples)

- Case study A — Fintech: "Payments.ai" (anonymized)
  - Problem: Real-time fraud scoring required sub-200ms inference for 99th percentile; existing self-hosted stack had high tail latency and high ops overhead.
  - Outcome: Migration to Redwood Dedicated reduced p99 latency from 480ms to 180ms, decreased cost per decision by 27% using batching and KV caching, and freed 2 FTEs previously dedicated to runtime maintenance.

- Case study B — Healthcare SaaS: "ClinicAssist" (anonymized)
  - Problem: PHI constraints meant hosted-only vendors were unacceptable; the customer required audit logs and a bring-your-own-key model.
  - Outcome: Redwood Private (VPC) with KMS integration enabled compliance, delivered a secure rollout in 8 weeks, and allowed the customer to scale to 200k monthly inference calls while meeting audit & retention requirements.

7) Security FAQ for prospect reviewers (short answers for engineering/security reviewers)

- Q: What compliance certifications do you hold?
  A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is in progress for ISO 27001 (anticipated completion Q3 2026). For Private deployments we provide evidence packages and assistance for customer audits.
- Q: How is customer data isolated in Dedicated and Private deployments?
  A: Dedicated pools provide tenant isolation at the GPU pool and control-plane level. Private deployments run in the customer VPC with optional on-prem packaging; control plane communications can be restricted to customer-managed networks.
- Q: How do you handle encryption and key management?
  A: Transit TLS 1.3 enforced; at-rest encryption using AES-256. We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and offer HSM-backed key handling for Private installs.
- Q: Do you retain prompts or outputs?
  A: Default retention for hosted accounts is 30 days for billing/observability; retention can be shortened or disabled for Paid Enterprise customers or on Private deployments. We provide data residency controls per-region.
- Q: How do you support logging and audit requirements?
  A: We provide configurable audit logs with token-level metadata, request/response hashes (where needed), and SAML + SCIM for identity integration. Logs can be routed to customer SIEM or stored in customer-managed storage for Private deployments.
- Q: What is your incident response posture?
  A: Eng-SRE maintains 24x7 on-call, published SLOs, and an incident runbook. We provide post-incident reports and can coordinate customer-facing communication plans for enterprise SLAs.

8) Enablement assets & playbook steps (for reps and AEs)

- Prep checklist before meeting:
  1. Confirm buyer personas and required security/compliance level.
  2. Obtain sample workload (RPS, seq length, model family) and run quick cost/latency estimate using internal estimator.
  3. Prepare one-pager and tailored pitch deck with case study aligned to prospect industry.
- Recommended POC approach:
  1. Security screening + NDA (1 week).
  2. POC kickoff (week 0): define success criteria (latency p50/p95/p99 targets, cost per 1k tokens, throughput).
  3. Technical validation (2–4 weeks): integration to Hosted API or Dedicated test pool, performance benchmarking, and security questionnaire completion.
  4. Pilot & scale (1–3 months): production-like load test, rollout plan, and pricing discussion.

Appendix: quick objection handling cheatsheet (short bullets)

- "We already have an LLM vendor": Ask about latency/cost pain and whether they run private deployments; pivot to economics + ops reductions.
- "We can self-host cheaper": Ask about TCO and hidden ops (FTEs, reliability, updates). Offer a short cost-model workshop.
- "We need strict data residency": Highlight Private deployment and KMS/HSM options and offer to schedule a technical deep dive with Eng-Private-Deployments.
